newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore trade on the cusp of recovery - economists. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Singapore trade on the cusp of recovery - economists. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]

text.p: Singapore's April non-oil exports will probably show and improvement, but economic recovery could be patchy as weak demand for electronics continues to stifle manufacturing, economists said on Monday.

A Reuter poll of 11 financial institutions revealed a more optimistic mood, producing an average forecast of a 0.5 percent rise for April non-oil domestic exports in nominal terms compared with a decline of 2.1 percent in March.
Economists said a combination of a high base comparison with April last year and a still anaemic manufacturing sector produced the relatively flat projection.
Forecasts ranged from a 3.1 percent drop to a three percent rise, a less negative slant in opinions than in recent polls.

"April will possibly be the last month of negative growth figures because last year we had a high comparison base," said Gan Chin Lee, an economist with Nikko Research who was among those who forecast another drop.
He said manufacturing was crimped by the semiconductor sector as the rise in U.S. orders had not filtered through to local producers.

"There's been a 38 percent rise in U.S. electronics orders, including semiconductors, in February and things should look up in the May export figures," he said. (Corrects quote to clarify views of economist)
Amanda Choy, an economist with Crosby Securities, agreed. Choy said she was confident of a recovery in the second quarter as semiconductor manufacturers were stepping up production.
"Local industry sources tell us utilisation levels are close to 100 percent in recent weeks," she said, adding that U.S. semiconductor figures looked healthy.
Manufacturing, the laggard sector, was seen propped up by strong performances in the finance and business sectors which should combine to support its recovery.
Maminder Singh, senior economist with Nomura Singapore, said a flat non-oil number still signalled an improved trade outlook.
"If you look at total manufacturing, it is up, quite a sharp increase from February," he said.
Economists generally blamed flat year-on-year percentage numbers in the first quarter to excess production last year, firms were ramping up output.
This fervour to meet anticipated demand later contributed to an overhang in inventory and decline in industry profits.
Singapore's electronics industry shrank 10.3 percent during the first quarter year-on-year, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said last week.
The electronics sector makes up about 25 percent of gross domestic product and nearly 60 percent of exports.
Most of the economists interviewed in the Reuter poll said an economic turnaround would take three to six months.
Kaan Quan Hon of DBS Securities said, however, that signs of a recovery were only stirring after five consecutive months of negative year-on-year growth.
"We should look at this month's figure to see if there is any momentum. Recovery is at a very early stage and demand is still weak," Kaan said.
